mainTopic: Supporting a stepdaughter, the millstone case and מדת סדום, the widow's housing and support, and רבי's last instructions
overview: The גמרא first explains why the food goes 'to the place where her mother is': a daughter stays with her mother at any age. It then tells of a millstone that was rented out in exchange for grinding. רבינא compares this case to the משנה, רב עוירא rejects the comparison, and the גמרא rules that if the renter has other grinding work, refusing to pay money is מדת סדום. A new משנה teaches that a widow may stay in her husband's house and be supported there, but the יורשים do not have to support her in her father's house unless she has a good reason. The גמרא spells out her rights: she keeps the same household use, the יתומים cannot sell her home, and a fallen house need not be rebuilt. Using רב הונא's rule that a full house is blessed, the גמרא concludes that a widow living elsewhere still gets the cheaper home amount. Finally, a ברייתא tells of רבי's last instructions to his sons and his summons of the חכמי ישראל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'to the place where her mother is'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we learn from the משנה's words 'to the place where her mother' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do we learn from the words 'to the place where her mother is'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא focuses on one phrase in the משנה and asks why it was needed. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a man who promised to support his wife's daughter must bring her food 'to the place where her mother' is. He cannot say, 'Come to my house and I will feed you there.' The גמרא wants to know why the משנה names the mother's place in particular, and what rule is hidden in those words.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Used here as 'what do we learn from…?'
To the place where her mother is

phrases.english: What is meant by 'to the place where her mother is'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the משנה from the previous section of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What rule is taught by the משנה's words 'to the place where her mother is'?

steps.title: A daughter stays with her mother at any age
steps.stepSummary: From these words we learn that a daughter lives with her mother, whether she is a גדולה or a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a daughter stays with her mother. It makes no difference whether she is an adult or a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The words teach that a daughter's place is with her mother, and this is true at every age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not split cases by age. It simply said the food goes to the mother's place. So the rule that a daughter stays with her mother covers a גדולה and a קטנה alike.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude from here
A daughter stays with the mother

steps.whatToRemember: A daughter stays with her mother, whatever her age. So the man who promised to support her must send the food to where the mother lives.

phrases.english: Learn from this: a daughter stays with the mother,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא גְּדוֹלָה וְלָא שְׁנָא קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: no difference whether she is an adult, and no difference whether she is a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase teaches that a daughter stays with her mother, whether she is a גדולה or a קטנה.

steps.title: Next משנה line: the two supporters may not share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the two men may not say that they will share her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'The two of them may not say…' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. It quotes the opening words to show which part it is now discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the woman's first husband and her second husband each promised to support her daughter. They may not say, 'We will split one portion between us.' Each man must give a full portion, because each one made his own complete promise.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on: the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: 'The two of them may not say,' and so on.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is that they may not say 'we will feed her together'; each one gives a full portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'mother's place' line to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two men who each promised to support the girl may not combine their obligations. Each must give a full portion.

steps.title: A millstone rented in exchange for grinding
steps.stepSummary: A man rented out his millstone, and the rent was paid by grinding for him. Later he became rich and bought his own millstone and a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who rented out a millstone to someone, and the payment was grinding. In the end, the owner became rich and bought another millstone and a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling a real case. This step lays out the facts that lead to the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rent was not paid in money. The renter paid by grinding the owner's grain. Now the owner has his own millstone and a donkey to turn it. That means he no longer needs the renter's grinding, and that is what sets up the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain man (the usual way a real case begins)

phrases.english: There was a certain man who rented out
a millstone to another man, for grinding.
phrases.notes: 'For grinding' means the rent would be paid by grinding the owner's grain, not with money.

phrases.english: In the end, he (the owner) became rich,
and bought a millstone and a donkey,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאוֹגַר לֵיהּ רִיחְיָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ לִטְחִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case is brought right after the משנה's line about obligations that cannot be changed or split.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: rent paid in grinding, and an owner who no longer needs the grinding.

steps.title: The owner wants money, the renter offers only grinding
steps.stepSummary: The owner asks for money now that he does not need grinding. The renter answers that he will keep grinding, as he agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner said to him: 'Until now I had my grinding done by you. Now, give me payment.' The renter said: 'I will grind for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The two sides state their claims. This sets up רבינא's attempt to decide the case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner argues that grinding was only a way of paying the rent. Since he no longer needs it, he wants the rent in money. The renter argues that the deal was grinding and nothing else. He is ready to keep his side of it, but he never agreed to pay money.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the renter as refusing to pay. He is offering to pay exactly as they agreed, in grinding. The argument is only about whether the owner can switch the payment to money.

phrases.english: He (the owner) said to him: Until now
I would have my grinding done by you,
now, give me payment.
He (the renter) said to him: I will grind for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד הָאִידָּנָא הֲוָה טָחֵינְנָא גַּבָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two sides' claims that come out of the facts in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner demands money. The renter insists on paying in grinding, as agreed. Steps 6 through 8 decide the case.

steps.title: רבינא compares the millstone case to the משנה about the two husbands
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests that the millstone case is just like the משנה where one man feeds the girl and the other pays her the value of the food in money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא wanted to say: this is the same as our משנה. Both men may not say 'we will feed her together.' Instead, one feeds her and the other gives her money for food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a proof from the משנה to decide the millstone case. He says the renter should now pay money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the second man promised food. Since she is already being fed, his promise turns into money. רבינא says the same here: the owner no longer needs grinding, so the promise to grind should turn into a money payment.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as our משנה

phrases.english: Ravina thought to say:
This is the same as our Mishnah:
Both of them may not say
'We will feed her together.'
Rather, one feeds her
and the other gives her the money value of food.
phrases.notes: רבינא's point: the renter should likewise switch from grinding to paying money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the owner-versus-renter argument from step 5 using the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the renter must now pay money instead of grinding.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: one man feeds the girl and the other pays her the money value of food.

steps.title: רב עוירא rejects the comparison: one stomach versus extra flour
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא says the cases are different. A girl can only eat one portion, but the owner can still use extra ground flour by selling it or storing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא said to him: Are the cases alike? There, she has one stomach, not two. Here, the renter can say to the owner: 'Grind and sell, grind and store.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא knocks down רבינא's proof. He shows that the two cases are not really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two men feeding one girl is truly useless, since she cannot eat double. That is why the promise has to turn into money. In the millstone case, the grinding still has value: the owner can sell the extra flour or save it, so the renter may keep his original deal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עַוִּירָא: מִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: Rav Avira said to him: Are the cases alike?
There, she has one stomach;
she does not have two stomachs.
Here, the renter can say to him:
'Grind and sell, grind and store.'
phrases.notes: He means: use your own new mill to grind for selling, and I'll keep grinding for you as we agreed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the two cases. It does not argue with the משנה itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Double feeding is useless, but extra grinding still has value for the owner.

steps.title: Limit: if the renter has other grinding work, he must pay money
steps.stepSummary: The renter may keep grinding only if he has no other use for the mill. If he does have other grinding work, refusing to pay money is מדת סדום, and the court forces him to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when the renter has no other grinding work for the mill. But if he has other grinding work for the mill, in a case like this we force him not to act with the trait of סדום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the ruling it just made, so we know exactly when the renter may keep grinding instead of paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the renter has no paying customers, grinding is the only way he can pay, so he may stick to the deal. If he has other customers, paying money costs him nothing extra. Refusing would only hurt the owner without helping himself, and that is מדת סדום, so the court forces him to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: The trait of סדום: refusing to help someone even when it costs you nothing

steps.whatToRemember: The renter may stay with grinding only if he has no other grinding work. If he has other work, refusing to pay money is מדת סדום, and the court forces him to pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the rule of כופין על מדת סדום: the court forces a person to give up a stubborn position that costs him nothing and only hurts someone else.

phrases.english: We only said this
when he has no other grinding for the mill;
but if he has other grinding for the mill,
in a case like this we force him
to stop acting with the trait of Sodom.
phrases.notes: So he must pay rent in money, since grinding for paying customers lets him earn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling from step 7, which let the renter keep grinding.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The renter may keep grinding only if he has no other grinding work. Otherwise the court forces him to pay money, because of מדת סדום.

steps.title: New משנה: a widow may insist on staying in her husband's house
steps.stepSummary: A widow who refuses to leave her husband's house cannot be sent to her father's house by the יורשים. They must feed her and give her a place to live that fits her dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow who said, 'I do not want to move from my husband's house': the heirs cannot say to her, 'Go to your father's house and we will feed you.' Rather, they feed her and give her living quarters that fit her dignity.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about where an אלמנה lives while she is being supported by her husband's יורשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יורשים must support the widow, but they might prefer that she live somewhere else. The משנה says the choice is hers. If she wants to stay in her husband's home, they must support her there, with housing fit for her standing.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A widow who said:
'I do not want to move from my husband's house,'
the heirs cannot say to her:
'Go to your father's house and we will feed you.'
Rather, they feed her
and give her living quarters fitting her dignity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new משנה about a widow's housing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a widow wants to stay in her husband's house, the יורשים must support her there and give her housing fitting her dignity.

steps.title: If the widow wants to stay in her father's house, the heirs can refuse to support her there
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a widow who insists on living in her father's house can be told by the יורשים that they will only support her if she lives with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said, 'I don't want to move from my father's house,' the heirs can say to her: 'If you live with us, you get food. If you don't live with us, you get no food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case from the one before. Now the widow is the one who wants to live away from the husband's house, in her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the יורשים could not push her out of the husband's house. Here she wants to leave, and the יורשים do not have to send her food wherever she chooses. The support she is owed comes with living in her husband's home.

phrases.english: If she said: 'I do not want to move from my father's house' —
the heirs can say to her:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתְּ אֶצְלֵנוּ — יֵשׁ לִיךְ מְזוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: If you are with us, you have food support,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין אַתְּ אֶצְלֵנוּ אֵין לִיךְ מְזוֹנוֹת.
phrases.english: and if you are not with us, you have no food support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה: אִי אֶפְשִׁי לָזוּז מִבֵּית אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse case of step 9: the widow, not the יורשים, wants her to live outside the husband's house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a widow refuses to live with the יורשים, they may refuse to support her elsewhere.

steps.title: Exception: she is young and the heirs are young
steps.stepSummary: If the widow's reason for leaving is that she and the יורשים are young, they must support her in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her claim was that she is young and they are young, they must feed her while she lives in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to the rule in step 10. If she has a proper reason, being young and living with young men, the יורשים must support her in her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 assumed she was leaving only because she preferred to. Here her reason is about modesty, since it is not proper for a young widow to live with young יורשים. Because she has a good reason, she does not lose her מזונות.
steps.whatToRemember: The widow's מזונות are tied to living in the husband's house. If she has a real reason to live elsewhere, such as being young along with young יורשים, they must support her in her father's house. Step 24 explains what she still gets even without such a reason.

phrases.english: If she was claiming
that it is because she is young and they are young —
phrases.notes: "They" means the יורשים. It is not proper for them all to live in one house.

phrases.english: they support her while she is in her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיְתָה טוֹעֶנֶת מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא יַלְדָּה וְהֵן יְלָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 10: a good reason for leaving keeps her support in place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A young widow living near young יורשים may live in her father's house and still receive מזונות.

steps.title: The widow keeps using the household as she did during her husband's life
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the widow uses the home, servants, bedding and silver and gold vessels just as she did while her husband lived, because the כתובה promised she would live 'in my house.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: She uses the living space the way she used it while her husband was alive. She uses the male and female servants, the pillows and blankets, and the silver and gold vessels the way she did while her husband was alive. This is because he wrote to her in the כתובה: 'You will live in my house and be fed from my property all the days you live as a widow in my house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that explains what 'living in her husband's house' means for the widow. She keeps the same level of living she had before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said she gets a home that fits her dignity. The ברייתא spells out the details: home, servants, bedding and valuable vessels all stay as they were. The source is the wording of the כתובה, which says she will live 'in my house' for as long as she is a widow.

keyTerms.meaning: the time you live as a widow

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a widow's rights come from the promise written in the כתובה. Because of that promise, her standard of living does not drop when her husband dies.

phrases.english: גמרא: The Rabbis taught:
She uses the living quarters
the same way she used them during her husband's lifetime.
The male and female servants,
the same way she used them during her husband's lifetime.
The pillows and blankets,
the same way she used them during her husband's lifetime.
The silver vessels and gold vessels,
the same way she used them during her husband's lifetime.
For this is what he wrote to her:
phrases.notes: This is quoting the wording of the כתובה.

phrases.english: 'And you will live in my house
and be fed from my property
all the days you live as a widow in my house.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins by spelling out what the widow's right to live in the house in step 9 includes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow keeps the same use of home, servants, bedding and vessels that she had during her husband's life, based on the כתובה's words 'in my house.'

steps.title: 'In my house' means a house, not a hut
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that the כתובה's words 'in my house' mean a proper house and not a small hut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: 'In my house,' and not in my hut.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reads one word of the כתובה closely. 'My house' means a real house, so a mere hut is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא based the widow's rights on the word 'בביתי.' רב יוסף sets a limit on that word: the right applies to a proper house. If the place is only a tiny hut, she cannot insist on living there with the יורשים.

phrases.english: רב יוסף taught:
'In my house' — and not in my hut.
phrases.notes: A hut is too small for her to share with the יורשים, so her right to live there does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּבֵיתִי וְלֹא בְּבִקְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the כתובה word 'בביתי' that the ברייתא in step 12 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow's right to live in the house applies to a proper house, not to a small hut.

steps.title: Orphans cannot sell the widow's home
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that if the יתומים sell the house where the אלמנה lives, the sale does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: If orphans sold the house a widow lives in, they did nothing. The sale does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a new rule: the heirs cannot sell the widow's home out from under her. If they try, the sale does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on what came before: the widow has a right to live in her husband's house. רב נחמן adds that this right is so strong that the house cannot be sold away from her at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They did nothing at all, meaning the act does not count

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Orphans who sold the widow's living quarters
did not do anything.
phrases.notes: In other words, the sale doesn't count, and she keeps living there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the widow's right to live in the house and adds that the heirs cannot sell it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale of the widow's living quarters by the יתומים does not count.

steps.title: Challenge from a case where the orphans' sale does count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this is different from רבי יוחנן's ruling that when יתומים sell from נכסים מועטין, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different here from what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן? רבי אסי said that רבי יוחנן said: If orphans went ahead and sold from a small estate, what they sold stays sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן by pointing to another case. There, the יתומים sold property that someone else had a claim on, and the sale still counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the heirs sell property that should have been held for someone else: the daughters in one case and the widow in the other. If the sale counts for the daughters, why should it fail for the widow?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to ask why two similar cases are treated differently
A small estate, where the daughters' support comes first
Who went ahead, acting first before the court could step in

phrases.english: And what is different
from what Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Orphans who went ahead and sold
from a small estate
phrases.notes: When the estate is small, it should be held back to support the daughters. The sons sold some of it before that could happen.

phrases.english: what they sold is sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִדְּרַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling from a parallel case
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that selling the widow's quarters does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a similar case, where heirs sell property meant to support the daughters, the sale counts. So why should the sale of the widow's home fail?

steps.title: The widow's claim started during the husband's life
steps.stepSummary: The daughters' claim only begins after the father dies, but the widow's claim on her home already existed while the husband was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the property was not tied to her during the father's lifetime. Here, the property was tied to her during the husband's lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a key difference in when each person's claim began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband had to give his wife a place to live even while he was alive, so the house was already tied to her before the heirs ever owned it. The daughters' right to support only starts when the father dies. Because the daughters' claim is weaker, the sons' sale can still go through in their case.

keyTerms.meaning: Are tied or pledged (like a lien) to someone
From the lifetime, meaning while the father or husband was still alive
There / here, used to compare two cases

steps.whatToRemember: The widow's right to her home began while her husband was alive, so the heirs cannot sell it. The daughters' claim began only at the father's death, so a sale from a small estate stands.

phrases.english: There, the property is not pledged to her from the father's lifetime,
phrases.notes: "Her" here means the daughters. Their claim only begins after the father dies.

phrases.english: here, it is pledged to her from the husband's lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by pointing to a difference between the two cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (timing of the claim)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases look the same, since heirs sell property that someone else has a claim on
steps.terutzMaskana: The widow's claim began during the husband's life, so it is stronger and blocks a sale. The daughters' claim began only at death, so it does not.

steps.title: No duty to rebuild a collapsed widow's house
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition that if the widow's house falls down, the יורשים do not have to rebuild it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that if a widow's living quarters collapsed, the heirs do not have to rebuild them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new rule about the widow's home: if the house collapses, the heirs do not have to build it again. The next step brings a ברייתא that supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a limit on the widow's housing right. Her right is to live in that specific house, the one tied to her. Once it is gone, the heirs do not have to put up a new building.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold by tradition, meaning we have received this ruling

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the widow's housing rights are cancelled in general. אביי is only saying the heirs don't have to rebuild that specific house.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We hold by tradition:
a widow's living quarters that collapsed
the heirs are not obligated to rebuild it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new rule about the limits of the widow's housing right
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the widow's house collapses, the heirs do not have to rebuild it.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי: a fallen house is not rebuilt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that the יורשים do not rebuild the widow's fallen house. It adds that she may not even rebuild it herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: if a widow's home falls down, the heirs do not have to rebuild it. More than that, even if she says, 'Let me rebuild it with my own money,' we do not listen to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the tradition אביי just reported in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats אביי's rule and then goes further. Even when the heirs would pay nothing, she still cannot rebuild. This shows that her right was tied to that specific house, and once the house is gone, the right is gone too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a phrase that brings support)
And not only that, but even more
We do not listen to her (her request is refused)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the issue is only who pays. Even when she offers to pay herself, she still may not rebuild. Her right to live there does not carry over to a new building.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
A widow's dwelling that fell down
the heirs are not obligated to rebuild it.
And not only that, but
even if she says,
"Leave me be, and I will rebuild it from my own,"
we do not listen to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's tradition from Step 17 with a ברייתא and adds a further rule.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's tradition that the יורשים do not rebuild the widow's fallen house
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the same rule and adding that she may not rebuild it even with her own money

steps.title: אביי asks about a house she only repaired, and the question stays open
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what the law is if the widow repaired the house. The question is left unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: if she repaired the house, what is the law? Let the question stand.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks about an in-between case: the house did not fully collapse, but she fixed it up. The גמרא cannot settle the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that she may not rebuild a fallen house. A repair falls between keeping the house as it is and rebuilding it. Is a repair treated like a rebuild, which would end her right, or may she stay since the house never stopped standing? No answer is found, so the question ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: She repaired it (fixed up the house)
Let it stand: the question is left unresolved

phrases.english: אביי asked:
If she repaired it, what is the law?
Let it stand.
phrases.notes: This means the question stays open. Nobody found an answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule about a fallen house and asks about the in-between case of a repaired house.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does repairing the widow's house count like rebuilding it, so that her right ends, or may she keep living there?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. The question remains תיקו.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the widow who says 'I don't want to'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a widow who refuses to leave her father's house and come live in her husband's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if she said, 'I don't want to.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a widow says she does not want to leave her father's house and asks the heirs to send her support there. The משנה rules that the heirs do not have to support her. Here the גמרא only quotes the opening words, and the next step will question the ruling.

phrases.english: She said: "I do not want to."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. She doesn't want to leave her father's house, so the heirs need not support her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the fallen-house discussion to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the widow refuses to move from her father's house, the heirs do not have to support her there.

steps.title: Why not send her the same support she would get at home?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the heirs should simply give her the same amount they would spend if she lived in her husband's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let them give her what she would get if she lived there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the heirs are fully free of her support. Why not just send her the amount she would cost them anyway?
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems the heirs lose nothing if they give her the same amount wherever she lives. So it looks unfair to cut off her support completely just because she lives somewhere else. The challenge assumes her cost is the same in both places.

phrases.english: But let them give her
as if she were living there?
phrases.notes: "There" means her husband's house, where she would normally live and be supported.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling quoted in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the heirs owe her nothing if she stays in her father's house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heirs could give her the same amount she would cost at home, so they lose nothing. Why exempt them completely?

steps.title: רב הונא: a full house is blessed, so living apart costs more
steps.stepSummary: The answer uses רב הונא's rule that a house is blessed when many people live in it. Supporting her apart costs the heirs more than supporting her at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב הונא, because רב הונא said: the blessing of a house comes with its many residents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Her cost is not really the same in both places, and the משנה is a support for רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When many people live together, each person costs less. So the heirs can say, 'Living with us, you cost us less than living on your own.' The challenge assumed the amount would be the same, and רב הונא's rule shows it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: In its abundance (in having many residents)

steps.whatToRemember: A shared home costs less per person (רב הונא: בִּרְכַּת הַבַּיִת בְּרוּבָּה). So the heirs do not have to pay the higher cost of the widow living elsewhere. Step 24 shows what they still owe her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the amount of the widow's support depends on where she lives. The heirs owe her the cost of living in the shared home, not the higher cost of living on her own.

phrases.english: This supports רב הונא.
For רב הונא said:
The blessing of the house is in its abundance.
phrases.notes: He means that with more people in one home, each person costs less, so living alone costs the heirs more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 by showing that her cost is not the same in both places.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the challenge's assumption is wrong: her cost is lower in the shared home
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her support costs the same wherever she lives, so the heirs should send it to her.
steps.terutzMaskana: Living together is cheaper (בִּרְכַּת הַבַּיִת בְּרוּבָּה), so the heirs need not pay the full, higher cost of her living elsewhere.

steps.title: Why not pay her what she would cost at home?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the heirs do not simply give the widow the amount she would cost if she lived in the family house, with the savings of a shared home already counted in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them give her support according to the 'blessing of the house,' meaning the smaller amount it would cost to feed her at home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on the answer it just gave. If supporting her apart costs more only because she loses the 'blessing of the house,' then the heirs should give her just the home amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 explained that the heirs may refuse because feeding her alone costs them more. The גמרא now pushes back: that extra cost can be avoided by paying her only what she would cost at home. So why should the heirs be allowed to stop supporting her altogether?

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing of the house: the savings that come when many people live together

phrases.english: But let them give her support
according to the blessing of the house?
phrases.notes: He means the smaller amount it would cost to feed her as part of the busy family home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 22 by suggesting a way to remove the heirs' extra cost.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the heirs may refuse to support the widow outside the family house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only problem is the extra cost, paying her the home amount removes the problem, so the heirs should not be exempt.

steps.title: Yes, that is what the heirs do
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: the heirs may give her only the home amount. The משנה did not mean they owe her nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, so it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the suggestion. The heirs pay her according to the 'blessing of the house' and nothing more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer changes how we read the משנה. When it says the heirs need not support her in her father's house, it means they need not pay the higher cost of living alone. They still give her what she would cost at home.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, so it is; the גמרא agrees with the suggestion

steps.whatToRemember: A widow who lives at her father's house is still supported, but only at the cheaper home rate.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as saying she loses her support completely. She only loses the extra amount that living apart would cost.

phrases.english: Indeed, so it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 23 and uses it to explain the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreement: the challenger's suggestion is the actual law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the heirs owe her no support at all in her father's house.
steps.terutzMaskana: The heirs give her the amount she would cost at home, figured with the blessing of the house.

steps.title: The words of the Sages bring blessing, wealth and healing
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that the wording of the חכמים hides lessons about blessing, wealth and healing. The lesson about blessing is the house rule just discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the language of the Sages is blessing, the language of the Sages is wealth, the language of the Sages is healing. 'Blessing' is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The house rule reminds the גמרא of a teaching by רב הונא. He gives three things we can learn from how the חכמים word their rulings, and he points to the first one right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's point is that the rulings of the חכמים also contain practical life advice. 'Blessing' is his own rule from step 22: a house with many people in it is blessed. The next two steps show the examples for wealth and healing.

keyTerms.meaning: The language or wording of the Sages

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The language of the Sages is blessing,
the language of the Sages is wealth,
the language of the Sages is healing.
Blessing: that which we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the rule that a house with many people in it is blessed (step 22).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves off the widow's case into a general teaching that is linked to the 'blessing of the house' idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wording of the חכמים teaches lessons about blessing, wealth and healing; the blessing lesson is the rule about a crowded house.

steps.title: Wealth: a smart tip for buying produce
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about buying produce shows how the חכמים teach a way to protect your money: rent the spot where the produce is sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wealth, as we learned: If someone sells produce to his friend, and the buyer pulled it but did not measure it, he has acquired it. If he measured it but did not pull it, he has not acquired it. And if he was smart, he rents the place where it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows רב הונא's second example, 'wealth,' using a משנה about buying produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer only owns the produce once he pulls it; measuring alone is not enough, so the seller could still back out. The משנה adds that a smart buyer rents the spot where the produce sits, so it is already in his own space and becomes his. That is money-saving advice tucked inside a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He pulled: an act of acquiring by drawing the item toward oneself
He acquired; it is now his

phrases.english: Wealth, as we learned:
One who sells produce to his friend,
if the buyer pulled it but did not measure it, he has acquired it;
if he measured it but did not pull it, he has not acquired it.
And if he was smart,
he rents its place.
phrases.notes: He rents the spot where the produce is lying, so it sits in a place that belongs to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second part of רב הונא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that the language of the חכמים teaches wealth
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about selling produce, which advises a smart buyer to rent the place of the produce

steps.title: Healing: chewed wheat on a wound
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about פסח forbids putting chewed wheat on a wound, which quietly shows that chewed wheat is a remedy for wounds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Healing, as we learned: A person should not chew wheat and put it on his wound on פסח, because it becomes חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows רב הונא's third example, 'healing,' using a משנה about פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is really about avoiding חמץ on פסח, since wet wheat becomes leavened. But by mentioning this case at all, it tells us that people put chewed wheat on wounds, so it must help them heal. A health tip is hidden inside a פסח law.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's three examples: blessing (a crowded house is blessed), wealth (rent the place of produce you buy), and healing (chewed wheat helps a wound).

phrases.english: Healing, as we learned:
A person should not chew wheat
and place it on his wound on פסח,
because they become leavened.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְפֵּא, דִּתְנַן: לֹא יִלְעוֹס אָדָם חִטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the third and last part of רב הונא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that the language of the חכמים teaches healing
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה forbidding chewed wheat on a wound during פסח, which hints that chewed wheat heals wounds

steps.title: רבי's last instructions to his sons
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records what רבי told his sons at the time of his passing: honor your mother, keep my lamp, table and bed in place, and my two attendants will keep serving me.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When רבי was passing away, he said, 'I need my sons.' His sons came in. He told them: 'Be careful to honor your mother. My lamp should stay lit in its place, my table set in its place, and my bed made up in its place. יוסף חפני and שמעון אפרתי served me in my lifetime, and they will serve me in my death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, a story of רבי's final words to his sons. This sets up the questions the גמרא will ask about each instruction, starting with the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic, separate from the widow's rights discussed earlier. רבי gives several instructions, and the very first one, honoring their mother, looks strange because the תורה already commands it. That puzzle drives the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They served me, they attended to me

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
At the time of Rebbi's passing,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: he said: I need my sons.
His sons came in to him.
He said to them: Be careful with the honor of your mother.
The lamp should be lit in its place,
the table should be set in its place,
the bed should be made up in its place.
Yosef Chofni and Shimon Efrati,
they served me in my lifetime,
and they will serve me in my death.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא and a new topic, after the earlier discussion of the widow and רב הונא's lessons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי commanded his sons to honor their mother, to keep his lamp, table and bed in place, and said his two attendants would keep serving him after death.

steps.title: Why command something the Torah already requires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי had to tell his sons to honor their mother when the תורה already commands honoring parents.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Be careful to honor your mother.' But that is a תורה law, as it says: 'Honor your father and your mother'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי's first instruction and challenges it. Why would he need to say something every Jew is already commanded to do?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that a dying great sage would not waste his last words repeating an obvious מצוה. So the instruction must be teaching something the sons would not already have known.

keyTerms.meaning: From the תורה, a תורה law
Honor your father and your mother

phrases.english: "Be careful with the honor of your mother."
But that is a Torah law,
as it is written: "Honor your father and your mother"!
phrases.notes: שמות 20:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first instruction in the ברייתא of step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's instruction 'Be careful with the honor of your mother.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה already commands honoring one's mother, so the instruction seems unnecessary.

steps.title: She was their stepmother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the woman was their father's wife, not their own mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: She was their father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the woman רבי meant was their stepmother, not the mother who gave birth to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'honor your mother' clearly covers a real mother. A stepmother is less obvious, so רבי had a reason to give a special warning.

phrases.english: She was a father's wife.
phrases.notes: Meaning she was their stepmother, married to רבי but not their own mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'mother' was a stepmother.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed 'your mother' meant their actual mother, whom the תורה already requires them to honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was their stepmother, so the instruction was needed.

steps.title: A stepmother must also be honored by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a ברייתא teaches that the extra words in the verse include a stepmother, a stepfather, and an older brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But honoring a father's wife is also a תורה law! A ברייתא teaches: 'Honor your father and your mother.' The extra word את before 'your father' includes your father's wife. The extra את before 'your mother' includes your mother's husband. The extra letter ו includes your older brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Even a stepmother is included in the תורה's command, so the question of why רבי needed to say it comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads small extra words in the verse as adding more people to the מצוה of honor. If a stepmother is already included, saying 'she was a stepmother' does not explain why רבי had to give the warning.

phrases.english: A father's wife is also a Torah law,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: "Honor your father and your mother":
"et your father": this is your father's wife,
phrases.notes: The word אֶת could be left out, so the ברייתא reads it as adding someone extra.

phrases.english: "and et your mother": this is your mother's husband,

phrases.aramaic: וָיו יְתֵירָה — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת אָחִיךָ הַגָּדוֹל!
phrases.english: and the extra vav: to include your older brother!
phrases.notes: This is the ו at the start of וְאֶת, meaning 'and'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵשֶׁת אָב נָמֵי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that she was their stepmother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא derives from the verse that a stepmother must also be honored by תורה law, so the instruction would still be unnecessary.

steps.title: Honoring a stepmother applies only while the father lives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the duty to honor a father's wife applies only during the father's lifetime, not after he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only while the father is alive, but after his death, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The תורה duty to honor a stepmother lasts only while the father is alive, so רבי, who was dying, had to tell his sons to keep honoring her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is accepted, but it is limited in time. After the father's death the תורה duty ends, which is exactly when רבי's instruction would matter. So his words were not extra after all.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (to this case only)

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה requires honoring a stepmother only while the father is alive. That is why רבי, on his deathbed, told his sons to keep honoring their stepmother after he was gone.
steps.confusionAlert: 'During life' and 'after death' refer to the father's life and death, not the stepmother's.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the duty to honor a stepmother comes from respect for the father, and it gives a source that this duty ends when the father dies.

phrases.english: This applies only during life,
phrases.notes: This means during the father's lifetime.

phrases.english: but after death, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי מֵחַיִּים, אֲבָל לְאַחַר מִיתָה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31 and backs up the answer of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a certain time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to require honoring a stepmother forever, which would make רבי's instruction unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה duty lasts only during the father's lifetime, so רבי had to command his sons to keep honoring her after his death.

steps.title: Why keep the lamp, table and bed in place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי's request about his lamp, table and bed, and asks what the reason was.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A lamp should be lit in its place, a table should be set in its place, a bed should be made up in its place." What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to another part of רבי's instructions and asks why he wanted these three things left as usual. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who has passed away does not need a lamp, a table or a bed. That is why the request sounds strange, and the גמרא wants to know what it was for.

phrases.english: "A lamp should be lit in its place,
a table should be set in its place,
a bed should be made up in its place."
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 28 to explain the next part of רבי's instructions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי wanted his lamp, table and bed to stay in their usual places after his death.

steps.title: He came home every Friday evening
steps.stepSummary: Even after his death, רבי returned to his house every ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every ערב שבת he would come to his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רבי kept coming home every ערב שבת even after he died, so he wanted his home set up as usual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strange request now makes sense. The lamp, table and bed were for real visits that רבי made after his death.

phrases.english: Every Shabbat eve
he would come to his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי הֲוָה אָתֵי לְבֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי returned home every ערב שבת after his death, so his things had to be ready for him.

steps.title: A neighbor nearly found out, so he stopped coming
steps.stepSummary: A neighbor knocked one Friday evening. The maidservant told her to be quiet because רבי was sitting there, and after that רבי stopped coming.
steps.simpleTranslation: On a certain ערב שבת a neighbor came and was calling at the door. His maidservant said: Be quiet, for רבי is sitting here. Once he heard that, he did not come again, so as not to bring a bad name on the earlier צדיקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רבי's visits came to an end: once his secret visits were about to become known, he stopped coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people knew that רבי came back after his death, they might think less of earlier צדיקים who never came back. To protect their honor, רבי gave up the visits.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring a bad name, to cast doubt on someone

steps.confusionAlert: רבי did not stop because something was wrong with visiting. He stopped only to protect the honor of earlier צדיקים who did not come back.

phrases.english: On a certain Shabbat eve a neighbor came,
she was calling at the door.
His maidservant said: Be quiet, for רבי is sitting here.
Once he heard, he did not come again,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל צַדִּיקִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
phrases.english: so as not to bring a bad name on the earlier righteous people.
phrases.notes: People might ask why those earlier צדיקים never came back like רבי did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 34 and tells how the visits ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי stopped visiting so that earlier צדיקים would not be thought less of.

steps.title: His two attendants will serve him, and the first understanding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי's words about יוסף חפני and שמעון אפרתי. People first thought he meant they would serve him in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: "יוסף חפני and שמעון אפרתי served me in my lifetime, and they will serve me in my death." People understood from this that he was talking about this world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last part of רבי's instructions and tells how people first understood it. This sets up the correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Serve me in my death" sounded like the two would take care of his burial in this world. This first reading will soon turn out to be wrong.

phrases.english: "Yosef Chofni and Shimon Efrati,
they served me in my lifetime
and they will serve me in my death."

phrases.aramaic: סְבוּר מִינָּה בְּהָדֵין עָלְמָא הוּא דְּקָאָמַר,
phrases.english: They understood from this that he was speaking about this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר מִינָּה בְּהָדֵין עָלְמָא הוּא דְּקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the last part of the ברייתא of step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first reading: the attendants would serve רבי in this world, at his burial.

steps.title: They died first, so he meant עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: When the attendants died before רבי, people realized he meant they would serve him in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they saw that their biers went before his bier, they said: Learn from this that he was speaking about that world.
steps.whatsHappening: Events showed that the first understanding was wrong. The attendants died before רבי, so he must have meant עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people who died before רבי could not serve him at his burial. So "in my death" must mean in the next world.

keyTerms.meaning: Their biers (the beds a body is carried on)

phrases.english: Once they saw that their biers went before his bier,
phrases.notes: In other words, the two attendants died before רבי did.

phrases.english: they said: Learn from this
that he was speaking about that world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first reading given in step 36.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי meant service in this world.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The attendants died before him, so they could not serve him at his burial.

steps.title: Why רבי said this about his attendants
steps.stepSummary: רבי said it so people would not claim the attendants died because of a fault, kept alive only by his merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he said this: so that people would not say, "There was something wrong with them, and until now it was רבי's merit that protected them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי spoke about his attendants: to protect their good name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without his words, people would think the attendants died because of sins once רבי's merit was gone. His words showed that they died first in order to serve him in עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's last wishes show care for others' honor. He stopped his visits for the sake of earlier צדיקים, and he spoke up for his attendants so no one would think badly of them.

phrases.english: And the reason he said this —
was so that people would not say: There was something wrong with them,
and until now, too,
it was רבי's merit that protected them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי made the statement that was clarified in steps 36 and 37.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי spoke about his attendants to protect their good name, so no one would think they died because of sins.

steps.title: רבי calls for the Sages of Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי says he needs the חכמי ישראל, and they come in to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I need the Sages of Israel. The Sages of Israel came in to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new scene: רבי asks for the חכמי ישראל, and they come into his room. This sets up the instructions he is about to give them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now רבי was speaking to the people close to him about personal matters. Now he calls for the leading חכמים, which signals that what comes next concerns the public and the community.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages of Israel, the leading Torah scholars
They came in to him, into his room

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲנִי צָרִיךְ.
phrases.english: He said to them: I need the Sages of Israel.
phrases.notes: "He" is still רבי, speaking near the end of his life.

phrases.english: The Sages of Israel came in to him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲנִי צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the explanation about רבי's attendants to a new scene, where רבי summons the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי summons the חכמי ישראל, and they come to him.

steps.title: Do not eulogize me in the small towns
steps.stepSummary: רבי's first instruction to the חכמים is that they should not eulogize him in the small towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Do not eulogize me in the small towns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי begins giving the חכמים his instructions, and the first one is not to hold eulogies for him in the small towns. This opens a list of instructions that continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first of the things רבי called the חכמים for. The instruction is about where eulogies for him should be held, and the גמרא continues his words right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: A eulogy, a speech mourning the dead

phrases.english: He said to them: Do not eulogize me in the small towns,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first instruction that רבי summoned the חכמים to hear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי instructs that he should not be eulogized in the small towns.
